title: 5 Internal Battles You Must Win First
paragraphs: 5 Internal Battles You Must Win First
You can’t lead others while losing wars nobody sees.

Some battles don’t scream in public.
They whisper in private.
And they can ruin a man long before sin ever becomes visible.
Here are 5 internal battles you must win first:

1. The battle with pride
Pride makes you feel strong while it quietly makes you unreachable.
You stop listening.
You stop repenting.
You start believing your own image.
But Scripture says, “God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble” (James 4:6).
Before God uses you greatly, He will humble you deeply.

2. The battle with lust
Lust is not just about the body.
It is the soul trying to feed a hunger only Christ can satisfy.
What you entertain in secret will eventually shape what you become in public.
Jesus does not just call us to manage lust. He calls us to crucify it.
Not by willpower alone.
By a heart surrendered to Him.

3. The battle with fear
Fear will make you delay obedience and rename it “wisdom.”
It will have you protecting comfort while calling it peace.
But many of us are not waiting on God.
We are hiding.
And God did not give you a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and a sound mind (2 Timothy 1:7).

4. The battle with bitterness
Bitterness feels justified.
That’s why it is dangerous.
It convinces you that holding the wound gives you control.
But it doesn’t heal you.
It chains you to the pain.
Forgiveness is not saying the wound was small.
It is saying Christ is greater.

5. The battle with unbelief
This one hides under church language.
You sing the songs.
You post the verses.
But deep down, you still doubt that God will come through.
Unbelief insults the character of a faithful God.
And that’s where grace walks in.
Jesus does not save perfect people with perfect faith.
He saves broken people who bring even their weakness to Him.

You will not win these battles by trying to become your own savior.
Self-help cannot cast out sin.
Discipline matters, yes.
But transformation begins at the cross.

Jesus took the penalty for your sin.
Jesus breaks the power of shame.
Jesus gives a new heart, not just better habits.
This is not behavior modification.
This is redemption.

So before you chase platforms, titles, influence, or applause—
win the war within.
And where you have already lost, run to Christ.
Not away from Him.

Because the Gospel is still this:
the blood of Jesus is strong enough for the battles nobody knows about.
